legacyMetricNotes.sharedGiftDecisions: Inherited count of chosen offering/starlibrary actions, including starlibrary study. It is not the number of permanent offering points. The exact chosen event counts are separated in cashLedger.byEvent.

talentMethod: Natural journeys fully fill all currently available finite priorities, then invest the remaining points in power. The priority labels describe ordering, not mutually exclusive trees. Same-start respec branches additionally expose focused templates which omit unrelated finite nodes; every point is still legally allocated.
cashMethod: Gross paid is computed from the legal action quote before its engine transaction. Gross receipts equal the committed gold change plus that payment. This captures immediate half-price refunds separately from net decreases and reconciles to final gold. No unobserved gold flows are inferred.
method: Fresh natural journeys. Every build finishes its explicit available talent priorities before progressing, including after paid respec; no points or items are granted. Item changes use the same current expected-upgrade estimate, not a claim of optimal item choice. Default conservative spending follows the earlier weapon-below-9/safe-material behavior. Forge-all raises all five equipped slots toward +20, retaining at least 20% of gold held on room entry (minimum80). Duplicate-materials adds explicit protected fusion only for weaker duplicate catalog IDs, retaining their strongest representative. All events take the first enabled adventurous choice.
abilityTriggerMethod: Counts the actual uniform abilityRoll trigger notes, plus phaseWard/firstCritLuck/eliteLuck/gildedSix conditions from each untouched pre-roll state and committed roll result. A fulfilled condition can hit a cap or be unnecessary in a one-shot battle; these are activation counts, not incremental realized utility.
limitations: This is policy sensitivity, not a player win-rate estimate, optimal strategy or a balance patch.
Different spending consumes different real dice; later RNG, routes, drops, events and talent histories may diverge. Whole-run differences are not attributed to one isolated stat.
Only forge counterfactuals explicitly assert equal enemy and combat-opening RNG; later kill timing may still change random consumption.
The expected-upgrade chooser omits some conditional interactions and survival value on relics; duplicate retention is an intentionally conservative collection preference.
The legacy spending columns remain net decreases. The separate cash ledger records gross payments and refunds; those two columns must not be added together.

Same-start respec branches deliberately hold gear fixed and compare only the next reachable battle. They use equal initial RNG, but luck, crit, healing, kill timing and later random consumption can still differ.
Fully learned finite trees cause priority builds to converge at sufficient point totals; that is a limit of this audit policy, not proof that players must choose the same build.
No price, enemy statistic, equipment identity, drop probability, RNG algorithm or production automation was changed.
